title: Extraction and Analysis of Structural Lineaments using Geospatial Techniques
author: Peter Emmanjay, Adaviruku
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Load DEM of study area
steps.instruction: Import the digital elevation model (DEM) covering the Adamawa sub‑catchment of the Upper Benue River basin into ArcGIS 10.8.

steps.title: Create hillshade layers
steps.instruction: Generate hillshade rasters from the DEM using the following Azimuth‑Altitude ratios: 315:45, 200:50, 150:65, and 100:60.

substeps.instruction: Set Azimuth = 315°, Altitude = 45° and produce hillshade.
Set Azimuth = 200°, Altitude = 50° and produce hillshade.
Set Azimuth = 150°, Altitude = 65° and produce hillshade.
Set Azimuth = 100°, Altitude = 60° and produce hillshade.

steps.title: Manually digitize structural lineaments
steps.instruction: Using expert visual interpretation, manually trace lineaments on each hillshade, extracting only structural lineaments and deliberately excluding geomorphological and pseudo‑lineaments.

substeps.instruction: Activate the digitizing tool and trace visible linear features that represent structural lineaments.
Repeat for the remaining hillshade rasters.
Review all traced features and delete any that correspond to geomorphological or artefactual patterns.

steps.title: Compile lineament map
steps.instruction: Combine all manually digitized lineaments into a single vector layer representing the complete lineament map for the study area.

steps.title: Calculate lineament statistics
steps.instruction: From the lineament map, compute lineament density (km / km²), total number of lineaments, and total length (km).

substeps.instruction: Use the ‘Calculate Geometry’ tool to obtain the length of each lineament.
Sum all lengths to obtain the total length.
Count the number of lineament features for the total number.
Divide total length by the catchment area to obtain density (range expected 1–5 km / km²).

steps.title: Generate rose diagram
steps.instruction: Create a rose (circular) diagram displaying the directional orientation trends of the extracted lineaments.

steps.title: Report results and interpretation
steps.instruction: Summarize the findings: 343 lineaments were identified with a total length of 2897.81 km; lineament density ranges between 1 km / km² and 5 km / km²; dominant orientations are N‑S, NNE‑SSW, NE‑SW, E‑W, SE‑NW, and SSE‑NNW.
